title: Correcting John Chilton's Who's Who entry on Lester Young's early years
summary: Dupre reads Chilton; Phillips says Lester was not drumming in 1920, left the family band in Salina not Phoenix, and left Bronson in Scott's Bluff, Nebraska in November 1930, not at Wichita.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Let me read this from John Chilton's book, Who's Who In Jazz, on Lester in that period. If you have any corrections, you can give them now. At that time, it says... Let me just go back a tiny bit earlier. What about Lester playing drums, by the way?
Phillips - 93
Oh, that's way back. That's when he was a little boy.
A little boy. I see. I'll start from the beginning, then read on. You add anything about this Bronson period, or anything at all that you want to add.
Okay.

"Born, Woodville, Mississippi, 27th August 1909. Brother of Lee Young. Their father W.H. Young, who had studied at Tuskegee Institute, tutored Lee, Lester and their sister Irma. Several other relatives were musicians, including the New Orleans trombonist-bassist named Austin "Boots" Young" [that's the one you mentioned, Boots] "and saxist Isaiah "Sport" Young. The family moved into New Orleans during Lester's infancy. He was taught trumpet, alto sax, violin and drums by his father. By the time the family had settled in Minneapolis, 1920..."
Lester?
Yeah, the first time, 1920. "...Lester was already playing drums with the family touring band, working through Minnesota, Kansas and Mexico, Nebraska and the Dakotas."
That's wrong.
That's wrong? That's before you joined, though.
Yeah. But in the 1920's, Lester wasn't up there then playin' no drums!
Well, the actual year 1920 it says.
Phillips - 94
All right.
And it says, "Lester was unwilling to tour the South, and left the band in Phoenix, Arizona..."
That's wrong.
...and he moved on to Salina, Kansas.
Hah-hah...

"Whilst at the Wiggly Cafe there, he met up with bandleader Art Bronson," [they don't give a year for this] "who bought him a tenor sax." Now, you say he didn't leave the band at Phoenix, Arizona and go on to Salina?
No, he left the band in Salina.
He met Bronson, it says here, at the Wiggly Cafe.
Yeah, he did meet him in a cafe.

It says here: "From January 1928 until ~January 1929, he did regular tours with Art Bronson's Bostonians, covering the Dakotas, Nebraska, Colorado, etc. He left Bronson to rejoin the family band, then rejoined Art Bronson from June to November of 1930."
That might have been. I know it was somewhere along 1930.
The first date was January 1928 to January 1929.
Yeah.
Then he left and then...
He came in 1930.
It says June to November 1930. Now we're getting a
Phillips - 95
little further on. It says, Bronson disbanded in Wichita, and Lester moved on to Minnesota."
That's wrong. Les wasn't even with Bronson then.
Wasn't with him when?
When we was in Wichita. He went with Bronson no more. He wasn't even with Bronson in Wichita. See, they said on that he disbanded, he left Bronson and went to Minneapolis.
Right.
He left Bronson in Scott's Bluff, Nebraska, and went to Minneapolis.
So that was in 1930.
1930. It must have been it was getting kind of cold when he left up there in Scott's Bluff.
